title: Epilepsy Treatment Access And Primary-Care Cascade Gaps In Low- And Middle-Income Countries
summary: Build a verified way to measure where people with epilepsy are lost between active disease, diagnosis, antiseizure-medicine initiation, uninterrupted refills, seizure control, and appropriate referral in low- and middle-income countries.
why_it_matters: Ministries of health, essential-medicines procurement authorities, and primary-care programme managers must decide whether scarce resources should first repair antiseizure-medicine continuity, task-shared diagnosis and follow-up, referral capacity, or community support. WHO reports around 50 million people living with epilepsy, nearly 80% in low- and middle-income countries, and a treatment gap of about three quarters in low-income countries, while up to 70% could become seizure-free with appropriate treatment. Yet a policy-maker cannot safely allocate against those figures unless observed data separate the active-epilepsy denominator from diagnosis, medicine possession, refill continuity, seizure control, and referral. A reviewed and replicated cascade would change that allocation decision without turning a modeled burden estimate, a medicine outlet survey, or a clinic registry into patient-level advice.

success_metrics.target: Every country or district artifact separates active-epilepsy definition, diagnosis, medicine initiation, refill continuity, seizure control, referral, and loss to follow-up with stage-specific denominators.
success_metrics.validation_method: A domain reviewer checks event grain, case definition, numerator, denominator, time reference, missingness, and whether each stage observes delivered care rather than policy or supply capacity.

success_metrics.target: Every antiseizure-medicine access result distinguishes policy listing, procurement, facility stock, dispensing, affordability, possession, and adherence rather than collapsing them into availability.
success_metrics.validation_method: A data reviewer maps each measure to a named source field and verifies that stock, dispensing, possession, and clinical outcome are not silently substituted for one another.

success_metrics.target: At least one independently replicated cascade artifact identifies a measurable programme bottleneck in a named setting without issuing patient-level diagnosis, prescription, or seizure-risk advice.
success_metrics.validation_method: A replicator reruns the documented analysis and red-team and field-reality reviewers confirm that the output remains within the observed setting and cannot be read as individual clinical guidance.

success_metrics.target: Every burden, pathway, medicine-access, or implementation claim links to a dated evidence record with method and explicit limitations.
success_metrics.validation_method: Run pnpm validate and spot-check every claim-to-source mapping in evidence.json and evidence.md.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, public-health and health-systems domain review, red-team review of clinical, privacy, and allocation misuse, field-reality review of the care pathway, and independent replication for quantitative outputs.
